papers.title_in_file: Implicit differentiation of variational quantum algorithms
papers.what_it_is: A paper showing how implicit differentiation gives gradients through variational quantum algorithms, with three small applications.

assertions.value: The authors state that a function defined implicitly as the solution of a quantum algorithm can be automatically differentiated using implicit differentiation, without regard to how the solution is computed.
quotes: A function defined implicitly as the solution of a quantum algorithm, e.g., a variationally obtained ground- or steady-state, can be automatically differentiated using implicit differentiation while being agnostic to how the solution is computed.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' general claim in the abstract; supported by their demonstrations.

assertions.value: The authors report that in a data-reuploading quantum classifier, the decision boundary with unoptimized hyperparameters seems to give worse validation performance than with hyperparameters optimized by implicit gradients, and state this avoids a costly grid search.
quotes: We can see that the decision boundary of the quantum classifier with an unoptimized set of hyperparameters seems to give a worse performance on a validation set compared to the case where hyperparameters are optimized.

We have shown that optimizing regularization strength using implicit differentiation could lead to better performance where implicit differentiation allowed a meta-optimization on the hyperparameters to avoid a costly grid search.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single small demonstration, one toy dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that their variational entanglement-generation algorithm is sensitive to the choice of loss function, optimization and hyperparameters, and that they demonstrate one choice that allowed creation of Bell states.
quotes: The algorithm is sensitive to the choice of the loss function, optimization, and hyperparameters and here we demonstrate one choice that allowed the creation of Bell states.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of a limit of the demonstration (Sec. 4.3).

papers.what_it_is: A paper proposing a quantum case-based reasoning scheme using a variational classifier and VQE, tested on the Social Workers' Problem.

assertions.value: The authors state that their qCBR improves on its classical counterpart in average accuracy, scalability and tolerance to overlapping data.
quotes: The focus is set on designing and implementing a qCBR based on the variational principle that improves its classical counterpart in terms of average accuracy, scalability and tolerance to overlapping.
We observed the outstanding performance of qCBR compared to its classical counterpart on the average accuracy, scalability and tolerance to an overlapping dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim; comparison on one problem family.

assertions.value: For 5 patients and 4 social workers, the authors report accuracy 92% for qCBR and 52.6% for the classical KNN-based CBR at case number 240 (Tables III and V).
assertions.anchor: Sec. VI, Tables III and V captions
quotes: The result of the qCBR for a number of patients and social workers fixed at 5 and 4, respectively.
And at the case number of 240, we will have an accuracy of 92%.
And at the case number of 240, we will have an accuracy of 52.6%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single study; the two captions use different circuit layers and validation schemes.
assertions.reader_inference: The two tables use different evaluation setups (qCBR depth 8; KNN CBR with 10-fold cross-validation), so the comparison is not like for like.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classical CBR designed with KNN behaves better for some determined cases.
quotes: it is observed that the classical CBR designed with the KNN behaves better for some determined cases
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of a limit of the advantage (Sec. VIII).

papers.title_in_file: Toward Quantum-Aware Machine Learning: Improved Prediction of Quantum Dissipative Dynamics via Complex Valued Neural Networks
papers.what_it_is: A paper showing that classical complex-valued neural networks predict quantum dissipative dynamics better than real-valued ones on spin-boson and FMO models.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the spin-boson model and Fenna-Matthews-Olson variants, complex-valued neural networks outperform real-valued ones in convergence speed, training stability and physical fidelity.
quotes: we demonstrate that CVNNs outperform RVNNs in convergence speed, training stability, and physical fidelity
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical benchmarks from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the 4-site FMO complex shows a twofold trace accuracy improvement for the CVNN over the RVNN.
quotes: The 4-site FMO complex (comprising the four prominent sites of the full 7-site system) already shows a twofold trace accuracy improvement for the CVNN over the RVNN.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single study result.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the spin-boson model neither model holds a decisive edge.
quotes: These offsetting advantages indicate that neither model holds a decisive edge for this minimally coherent system.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one study.

papers.title_in_file: Strategies for running the QAOA at hundreds of qubits
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of QAOA with fixed tree parameters and warm starts on MaxCut for random 3-regular graphs.

assertions.value: The authors provide extensive numerical evidence that approximation ratios with tree parameters are typically well beyond the conjectured lower bounds.
quotes: We provide extensive numerical evidence supporting the performance guarantee for tree parameters conjectured in [WuLo21] and see that the approximation ratios obtained with tree parameters are typically well beyond the conjectured lower bounds.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerics on random instances.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerics on random instances do not provide general performance guarantees but provide substantial evidence of a regime where QAOA finds good solutions at low depth without parameter optimization.
quotes: Our numerics on random instances do not provide general performance guarantees but do provide substantial evidence that there exists a regime of instance sizes in which the QAOA finds good solutions at low depth without the need for parameter optimization.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of the limit of their evidence (Abstract).

assertions.value: The authors state they restrict attention to MaxCut on 3-regular graphs and problem sizes of up to 512 vertices, and that expected cut sizes are computed classically while producing actual cuts requires a quantum computer.
quotes: We restrict our attention to MaxCut on 3-regular graphs and on problem sizes of up to 512 vertices.
For each instance studied, we classically compute the expected size of the QAOA distribution of cuts; producing the actual cuts requires running on a quantum computer.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of setup and scope.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Embeddings for Many Body Quantum Systems
papers.what_it_is: A paper proposing a variational embedding scheme combining classical and quantum solvers for many-body quantum systems.

assertions.value: The authors state they demonstrate the protocol on spin chains and small molecules and have successfully tested the method on spin systems and molecular Hamiltonians.
quotes: We demonstrate the effectiveness of the protocol on spin chains and small molecules and provide insights into its accuracy and computational cost.
We have successfully tested our method on spin systems and molecular Hamiltonians, demonstrating its potential.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author-reported demonstrations, mostly simulated.

assertions.value: The authors state that the effect of hardware noise on the results should be investigated, so it is not studied in the paper.
quotes: Under the quantum computation perspective, the effect of hardware noise on the results should be investigated.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of an open limit (Discussion).

papers.title_in_file: Solving General QUBOs with Warm-Start QAOA via a Reduction to Max-Cut
papers.what_it_is: A paper comparing two warm-start QAOA approaches for general QUBOs, one via reduction to Max-Cut.

assertions.value: The authors find that the best choice of warm-start approach is strongly dependent on the problem type.
quotes: We find that the best choice of warmstart approach is strongly dependent on the problem type.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors state they compare the two warm-start approaches for a variety of QUBO types up to 16 variables.
quotes: We empirically compare the two warm-start approaches above for a variety of different types of QUBOs up to 16 variables.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of setup and scope (Sec. 1).

assertions.value: The authors state that the performance of QUBO-Relaxed is strongly dependent on the number of random initial conditions tested.
quotes: Because QUBO-Relaxed relies on a non-QUBO-Relaxed optimization problem, its performance is strongly dependent on the number of random initial conditions tested by the optimizer.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement; supported by their runs.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Optimization for the Future Energy Grid: Summary and Quantum Utility Prospects
papers.what_it_is: A project summary of Q-GRID benchmarking quantum and classical optimization for energy grid problems.

assertions.value: The authors report exponential classical optimizer runtime scaling for select energy grid problems and initial findings that QAOA and hybrid quantum annealing solvers may give more favourable runtime scaling for similar solution quality.
quotes: For select energy grid optimization problems, we demonstrate exponential classical optimizer runtime scaling even for small problem instances, and present initial findings that variational quantum algorithms such as QAOA and hybrid quantum annealing solvers may provide more favourable runtime scaling to obtain similar solution quality.
assertions.certainty_reason: Initial findings of one project, stated as such.

assertions.value: The authors report a crossover in performance between Gurobi and the Leap hybrid solver between 100 and 200 customers, and note that the comparison is not directly fair.
quotes: a crossover in performance between Gurobi and Leap happens between 100 and 200 customers. After that size, Gurobi cannot find converged results in the given time limit.
Although not a directly fair comparison since Gurobi is run on a local machine whilst the Leap hybrid solver is run on a proprietary D-Wave cloud architecture.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single benchmark with an acknowledged unfair hardware comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum approaches may provide some advantages but that further investigation is needed to explore any evidence of potential quantum utility in the energy sector.
quotes: We have demonstrated that quantum optimization approaches may provide some advantages over traditional classical optimization approaches in terms of application-specific benchmarks or hybrid algorithm solution quality, however further investigation is needed to explore any evidence of potential quantum utility in the energy sector.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of the limit of their conclusion (Sec. 6).

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm in Finite Size and Large Depth and Equivalence to Quantum Annealing
papers.version_note: Title in the file (v2, Oct 2025) differs from the record's file name (Equivalence of QAOA and Linear ...), but the arXiv id 2503.09563 matches; read as the same paper.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Theorem III.4 statement, discussion and limitation section.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving that QAOA with smoothly varying, bounded-sum angles approximates linear-time quantum annealing on the SK model.

assertions.value: The authors prove that if the angles are smaller than an absolute constant independent of instance size, QAOA achieves energy density arbitrarily close to that of quantum annealing with the corresponding schedule for sufficiently large depth, for the disorder-average on the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model.
quotes: Specifically, we prove that if the angles are smaller than an absolute constant independent of the instance size, QAOA achieves energy density arbitrarily close to that of quantum annealing with corresponding schedule for sufficiently large depth
More precisely, we prove this equivalence result for the disorder-average of the energy density achieved by QAOA on the SherringtonKirkpatrick (SK) model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem III.4, Sec. III A.

assertions.value: The authors state that the equivalence holds under two conditions: angles vary smoothly from one layer to the next and their sum is bounded by a constant.
quotes: we provide evidence against this by analytically showing that QAOA energy approximates that of quantum annealing under two conditions, namely that angles vary smoothly from one layer to the next and that the sum is bounded by a constant.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conditions of the proved result, Abstract and Theorem III.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that an important limitation of their findings is the restriction to gradually varying QAOA angles, and that if it is relaxed, exponential separations exist between QAOA and quantum annealing.
quotes: An important limitation of our findings is their restriction to gradually varying QAOA angles.
If this restriction is relaxed, exponential separations exist between the performance of QAOA and quantum annealing [39].
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' stated limit, Discussion p.17.
